cards.scientific_scope: Real homogeneous quartics F=alpha H+beta u^2+gamma j^2+delta uj on 2x2 matrices, H=((a-d)^2+(b+c)^2)^2, u=a^2+c^2, j=det A; existence of finite alpha after deleting that coordinate.
cards.statement: Some finite alpha makes F ROC iff some finite alpha makes it all-background QC iff either delta=0 with beta,gamma>=0, or delta!=0, gamma>0, 6beta gamma-delta^2+delta gamma>=0 and 2beta+delta>0. For q=r(r+2)>0, the exact universal isotropic construction supplies a finite c(r) with P_(c(r),r) QC and, for alpha>=c(r), Jensen gap >=4(alpha-c(r))/1875 times integral|Dphi|^4. Every finite P_(alpha,r) with r(r+2)!=0 is ordinarily non-polyconvex, even allowing arbitrary nonsmooth nonpolynomial convex lifts. The same local obstruction survives every everywhere-finite C3 correction flat through degree three at I. On the nonzero curved projected boundary, finite QC completion exists while finite ordinary-PC completion does not. QC at the positive sharp floor remains UNKNOWN.

cards.statement: Under the additive corrected scattering model, M=integral nnT dV, f=traceM and W=integral S^2 nnT dV are distinct targets. Fixed x/y populations of volume1/2 with S=(4/5,2/5), then swapped, have unchanged M and total intensity while normalized intensity contrast changes by6/5. For unrestricted unit axes and supplied0<s<1 with s<=S<=1 plus acquired W and f, the exact identified set is s^2M<=W<=M, traceM=f; spectral atoms of P=(W-s^2M)/(1-s^2),R=(M-W)/(1-s^2) attain every feasible pair. Known finite axis support instead requires the exact m_i,w_i mixture LP. At s=2/5,f=1 the two-arm volume contrasts are[0,21/25] and[-21/25,0], so their difference can be0 despite intensity difference6/5. Without a uniform floor but0<S<=1, fixed-W feasibility additionally requires equal supports; dropping that condition gives joint-pair closure when W varies, not closure of a fixed-W fiber.
